name: Chapter 9: Amines
description: Structure, naming, preparation, basicity, carbylamine and Hinsberg tests, aniline substitution, diazonium salts and coupling

cards.definition: Derivatives of ammonia in which one, two or three H are replaced by alkyl/aryl groups

cards.text:
Amines in use: {{c1::adrenaline and ephedrine}} (2° amino) raise blood pressure
{{c2::novocain}} is a dental anaesthetic
{{c3::benadryl}} (3° amino) is an antihistamine
quaternary ammonium salts are {{c4::surfactants}}.

cards.definition: N is sp³; shape pyramidal, one orbital holds the lone pair

cards.term: C–N–C angle in trimethylamine and why?
cards.definition: 108° (< 109.5°): lone pair repulsion
One, two, three H of NH₃ replaced: RNH₂, R₂NH, R₃N
Simple: all groups the same. Mixed: different groups.
No: it is a primary amine (one C on N); amine class counts groups on N, not the carbon type
Primary: alkanamine (replace "e" by "amine": methanamine). 2°/3°: prefix N- for groups on N.
Table 9.1
8: butan-1-amine, butan-2-amine, 2-methylpropan-1-amine, 2-methylpropan-2-amine (1°) N-methylpropan-1-amine, N-methylpropan-2-amine, N-ethylethanamine (2°) N,N-dimethylethanamine (3°)
Chain, position and metamerism (and functional between classes)
H₂ with Ni/Pd/Pt, or metal + acid (Sn/HCl, Fe/HCl)
FeCl₂ formed hydrolyses to release HCl, so only a little acid is needed to start
R–X + ethanolic NH₃ in sealed tube at 373 K: SN, C–X cleaved by NH₃
Gives a mixture of 1°, 2°, 3° amines and quaternary salt; use large excess NH₃ for 1°

cards.term: Getting the free amine from its salt?
cards.definition: Treat with strong base (NaOH)
RI > RBr > RCl

cards.term: Example 9.1: C₂H₅Cl + NH₃; benzyl chloride + NH₃ then 2 CH₃Cl?
cards.definition: Ethanamine → N-ethyl... → quaternary salt; benzylamine → N,N-dimethylphenylmethanamine
LiAlH₄ or H₂/Ni → 1° amine R–CH₂NH₂: ascends the series by one C
LiAlH₄ then H₂O → R–CH₂–NH₂ (same C count)
Phthalimide + ethanolic KOH → K-phthalimide + R–X → N-alkylphthalimide alkaline hydrolysis → pure 1° amine
NaOH(aq) → sodium phthalate + R–NH₂
Aryl halides don’t undergo SN with phthalimide anion
RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → R–NH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O: amine has one C fewer
The alkyl/aryl group moves from carbonyl C to N

cards.term: Example 9.3: amide giving propanamine; amine from benzamide?
cards.definition: Butanamide; aniline
Ethanolic NaCN (→ nitrile), then reduction
Nitration then Sn/HCl; then aniline + 2CH₃Cl
KCN (→ NC(CH₂)₄CN), then LiAlH₄ / H₂-Ni

cards.definition: Nitrile reduction (R–X → RCN → RCH₂NH₂): +1 C; Hoffmann bromamide: −1 C; Amide reduction (LiAlH₄): Same; Gabriel synthesis: Same (1° only)

cards.term: Physical state and smell of amines?
cards.definition: Lower aliphatic: gases, fishy odour ≥3 C (1°): liquids higher: solids

cards.term: Why does aniline darken on storage?
cards.definition: Atmospheric oxidation
H-bonding with water; falls as the hydrophobic alkyl part grows

cards.term: More soluble in water: butan-1-ol or butan-1-amine?
cards.definition: Butan-1-ol: O (3.5) more electronegative than N (3.0), stronger H-bonds

cards.term: b.p. order of isomeric amines and why?
cards.definition: 1° > 2° > 3°: 1° has two N–H for H-bonding; 3° has none

cards.term: b.p. of butan-1-amine vs butan-1-ol vs alkane?
cards.definition: n-C₄H₉NH₂ 350.8 K (C₂H₅)₂NH 329.3 C₂H₅N(CH₃)₂ 310.5 alkane 300.8 n-C₄H₉OH 390.3 K
Form ammonium salts (aniline + HCl → anilinium chloride); NaOH regenerates amine
Salts are water-soluble, ether-insoluble: separate amines from non-basic compounds
Lone pair on N
R–NH₂ + H₂O ⇌ R–NH₃⁺ + OH⁻; larger Kb / smaller pKb = stronger base

cards.term: pKb of ammonia? Aliphatic amines? Aniline?
cards.definition: 4.75; 3–4.22 (stronger); aniline 9.38 (much weaker)

cards.term: Why are alkylamines stronger bases than NH₃?
cards.definition: +I of alkyl pushes electron density to N and stabilises the cation

cards.term: Basicity order in the gas phase?
cards.definition: 3° > 2° > 1° > NH₃ (inductive only)

cards.term: Why is the aqueous order different?
cards.definition:
Cation also stabilised by H-bonding with water (solvation): the 1° cation has most N–H (best solvated)
Plus steric hindrance

cards.text: Aqueous basicity: methyl series {{c1::(CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > (CH₃)₃N > NH₃}}; ethyl series {{c2::(C₂H₅)₂NH > (C₂H₅)₃N > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃}}.

cards.term: Memory hook for the aqueous order?
cards.definition: Secondary always wins. Methyl: 2 > 1 > 3 (small CH₃ lets water solvate 1° well, 3° worst). Ethyl: 2 > 3 > 1 (bulky ethyls make +I matter more).

cards.term: Why is aniline a weaker base than NH₃?
cards.definition:
N lone pair is delocalised into the ring (5 resonance structures).
Anilinium has only 2, so protonation loses stabilisation
EDG (–OCH₃, –CH₃) increase; EWG (–NO₂, –SO₃H, –COOH, –X) decrease
(C₂H₅)₂NH > C₂H₅NH₂ > NH₃ > C₆H₅NH₂

cards.term: Increasing basicity (Intext 9.4 i): C₂H₅NH₂, C₆H₅NH₂, NH₃, C₆H₅CH₂NH₂, (C₂H₅)₂NH?
cards.definition: C₆H₅NH₂ < NH₃ < C₆H₅CH₂NH₂ < C₂H₅NH₂ < (C₂H₅)₂NH

cards.term: Why is benzylamine (pKb 4.70) much stronger than aniline?
cards.definition: CH₂ separates N from the ring: no resonance of the lone pair
With R–X → higher amines and finally quaternary ammonium salt
N,N,N-Trimethylanilinium iodide (quaternary)
1° and 2° amines + acid chloride/anhydride/ester → amides; base (pyridine) removes HCl
No: no H on N
Amine + C₆H₅COCl: methanamine → N-methylbenzamide; aniline → benzanilide

cards.term: Amines + carboxylic acids at room temperature?
cards.definition: Form salts
1° amine + CHCl₃ + ethanolic KOH, heat → foul-smelling isocyanide; 2° and 3° don’t react
Unstable diazonium salt → N₂ (quantitative) + alcohol; used to estimate amino acids and proteins
Benzenediazonium chloride (diazotisation)

cards.term: Isomers of C₃H₉N giving N₂ with HNO₂ (Intext 9.8)?
cards.definition: Only the 1° amines: propan-1-amine, propan-2-amine
Benzenesulphonyl chloride C₆H₅SO₂Cl (now often p-toluenesulphonyl chloride)
N-Ethylbenzenesulphonamide: N–H is acidic (strong EWG SO₂) → soluble in alkali
N,N-Diethylbenzenesulphonamide: no N–H → insoluble in alkali
No reaction
Carbylamine (CHCl₃/KOH): Foul smell · none · none; Hinsberg product in alkali: Soluble · insoluble · no reaction; HNO₂ (aliphatic): N₂ + alcohol · different · different

cards.definition: Powerful activating, o/p-directing
White ppt of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (at room temperature)
Protect –NH₂ by acetylation (acetanilide), brominate (Br₂/CH₃COOH → p-bromo major), hydrolyse
N lone pair is also delocalised onto the C=O oxygen
Tarry oxidation products + p (51%), m (47%), o (2%)
In strong acid aniline becomes anilinium ion, which is meta-directing
Acetylate → nitrate (p-nitroacetanilide) → hydrolyse
Conc. H₂SO₄ → anilinium hydrogensulphate; 453–473 K → sulphanilic acid (exists as zwitter ion)
Aniline forms a salt with AlCl₃; N⁺ strongly deactivates the ring

cards.term: General formula and naming of diazonium salts?
cards.definition: \( ArN_2^+X^- \); e.g. benzenediazonium chloride, benzenediazonium hydrogensulphate

cards.term: Why are arenediazonium salts more stable than alkyl ones?
cards.definition: Resonance with the ring
Aniline + NaNO₂ + 2HCl at 273–278 K; used immediately

Colourless crystalline, water-soluble, stable cold, reacts with warm water; decomposes dry.
Fluoroborate is insoluble and stable at room temperature
ArN₂⁺ + Cu₂Cl₂/HCl, Cu₂Br₂/HBr, CuCN/KCN → ArCl, ArBr, ArCN + N₂
ArN₂⁺ + HX with Cu powder → ArX; yield lower than Sandmeyer
Just KI
HBF₄ → ArN₂⁺BF₄⁻ ppt; heat → Ar–F
Mild reductants: H₃PO₂ or ethanol (oxidised to H₃PO₃ / ethanal)
Let temperature rise to 283 K (warm with water)
Fluoroborate + aq. NaNO₂ / Cu, heat
Para coupling (alkaline) → p-hydroxyazobenzene (orange dye)
(acidic) → p-aminoazobenzene (yellow dye)

cards.term: What type of reaction is coupling? Why coloured?
cards.definition: Electrophilic substitution; extended conjugation through –N=N– (azo dyes)

cards.term: Why are diazonium salts so useful in synthesis?
cards.definition: Introduce –F, –Cl, –Br, –I, –CN, –OH, –NO₂ where direct substitution fails (Ar–F, Ar–I, Ar–CN)
Br₂/Fe → Sn/HCl → diazotise → H₃PO₂ (remove N) → KMnO₄
Br₂/H₂O → 2,4,6-tribromoaniline diazotise H₃PO₂ removes the N group
Diazotise, then HBF₄, then NaNO₂/Cu (replace by NO₂)
CuCl/HCl: ArCl (Sandmeyer); CuCN/KCN: ArCN; KI: ArI; HBF₄, heat: ArF; H₃PO₂ or C₂H₅OH: ArH; H₂O, 283 K: ArOH; Phenol (OH⁻): p-Hydroxyazobenzene
